author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read Commvault CommServe syslog of events, the audit trail and alerts. CommServe sends them over UDP or TLS as syslog to the data collector, in batches about every eight minutes. Audit trail logins, logouts, login failures and lockouts go to Auth; alerts and anomaly (ransomware) detections go to the third-party alert schema; other audit records and events go to ManagementEvent.
notes:
Setup:
- CommServe syslog forwarding of events, the audit trail and alerts, over UDP or TLS, which Commvault sends in batches about every eight minutes.
- Commvault publishes the RFC 5424 form in its log streaming templates; turn it on with the bUseRFC5424FormatInSyslog additional setting (11.36 and later).
- The parser also reads the default Key = {value} form of events and the audit trail, which Commvault doesn't document.

Field mapping:
- Logins, logouts, login failures and lockouts from the audit trail go to Auth.
- Alerts, and the anomaly (ransomware) detections CvStatAnalysis raises as event code 14:337, go to the third-party alert schema with the file counts from the anomaly description.
- Other audit records and events go to Management Event, with the Commvault severity as result.

Time:
- The event time comes from Utctimestamp; a record without it has only the CommServe's local time, which is read as UTC.

Sources and licenses:
- The default Key = {value} shape comes from lines on Commvault's community site.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples are made up in these shapes.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-14 (120 of 120 fields matched the emulator in each of 5 runs), and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there.
- Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent.
- No built-in parser claimed these lines.

Known gaps:
- No public example of a default-form alert exists, so those aren't covered.
- Syslog alerts carry no severity.
